summary: Jitsushyu Oshika is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. Oshika served as a professor at Toyo University (attested 1980–1981).

Jitsuzo Kuwabara worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1896), Kuwabara held posts at the Third Higher School (1898–1899), Tokyo Higher Normal School (1899–1907), and Kyoto Imperial University (1909–1930).
Jiun Kubota is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Kubota studied under traditional teacher Kyozo Yamada (~1970–1989) and succeeded Koun Yamada.

Jivnesh Sandhan works in computational linguistics and Indology, earning a PhD at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur under Laxmidhar Behera. Sandhan held posts at UC Berkeley, IIT Kanpur, Kyoto University, and IIT Dharwad (attested 2025).

Jiyu Ren worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, studying at Peking University under Lin He and Yongtong Tang. Ren held posts at Peking University (1942–1964), CASS (from 1956; director 1964–1986), and the National Library of China (1987–2005).

Jiyu-Kennett was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Durham University, Trinity Laban, and Soji-ji under teachers including Seck Kim Seng and Keidō Chisan Kōho. Kennett served as head priest at Unpukuji and abbess of Shasta Abbey (1970–1996).
Joachim Friedrich Sprockhoff is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Friedrich Otto Schrader and Helmuth von Glasenapp.

Joachim Gentz works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. Gentz served as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and held posts as Reader (attested 2013) and Professor (attested 2026) at the University of Edinburgh.

Joachim Heidrich was an Indologist and historian who earned a Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Walter Ruben. Heidrich held posts at the Zentralinstitut für Geschichte (1981–1989) and the Leibniz-Zentrum Moderner Orient (~1992–1995).

Joachim Menant was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at the University of Caen Normandy. Menant held a post at the University of Paris and became a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres in 1888.
Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and earned a Magister degree at the University of Vienna.

Joachim Wach worked in religious studies and philosophy, studying at Leipzig, Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, and Heidelberg. Wach held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (1924–1935), Brown University (1935–1946), and the University of Chicago (1945–1955).

Joan Jiko Halifax works in Buddhist and religious studies, holding degrees from Newcomb College and Union Institute & University. Halifax held posts at Columbia, Miami, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, Harvard, and the Library of Congress, and founded the Upaya Zen Center.
Joan Mascaró was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1926–1929). Mascaró served as Professor of English at the University of Barcelona in 1933.

Joanna Bialek is a Tibetologist and linguist who completed a PhD at the University of Marburg. Bialek held postdoctoral and research positions at Humboldt University of Berlin (2017–2022), Trinity College Dublin (2024–2026), and the University of Munich (2026).
Joanna Cook is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under advisor James Laidlaw. Cook held a post at Christ's College, Cambridge.

Joanna Gottfried Williams was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University. Williams served on the faculty at the University of California, Berkeley, from ~1971 to 2022, including as professor.

Joanna Grela is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from INALCO, Jagiellonian University, and SWPS University. Grela was appointed as a professor (profesor UJ, dr hab.) at Jagiellonian University in 2006.
Joanna Macy is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who completed her education at Wellesley College (~1946–1950) and Syracuse University (~1973–1978).

Joanne Punzo Waghorne is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Chicago. Waghorne held posts at UMass Boston (1975–1983), Bowdoin College (1983–1985), UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University.
